name: Largest Recovered Layer Set of an Ample Obstruction
statement: For an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor $X$, call nonempty $E\subseteq\mathcal B(X)$ successful when it satisfies the distinct-singleton recovery criterion, without requiring a cornerless seed. Successful sets are closed under union. Thus, whenever recovery is possible, there is a unique largest successful set $E_{\max}(X)$, equal to the set of balanced coordinates whose singleton-start forced-enlargement procedure succeeds. Its recovered seed $X^{E_{\max}(X)}$ is determined by $X$ independently of any presentation choice.
proof: Recover a presentation on one successful set $E$. Its seed is again an irredundant ample forbidden pc-minor, and signed-clause transport shows that balanced coordinates outside $E$ remain balanced in the seed. For a disjoint successful set $D$, singleton fibres force every seed clause meeting $D$ to come from one of two outer repairs whose owner supports equal all of $E$. These two blocks exhaust the signed $E$-facets and have antipodally punctured rows. The induced fibres in the seed are distinct singletons, so nested recovery makes $E\cup D$ successful. For overlapping $E,D$, strongly project their intersection. Their differences become disjoint successful sets in an irredundant forbidden reduction; applying the disjoint argument there and lifting by nested recovery again yields $E\cup D$. Finiteness makes the union of all successful sets successful. A coordinate belongs to this union exactly when its singleton-start closure succeeds, giving the formula and canonical seed.
comments: Union closure uses obstruction minimality and is false for arbitrary ample families; the certificate includes a six-word peelable counterexample. Six certified obstruction models check disjoint and overlapping unions, signed seed-coordinate inheritance, and recovery of the largest set from singleton starts.
